scope: Fifth isolated read-only diagnostic, adding finite static technical tokens to the previously sanitized errors. No arbitrary error text, credential/business values, configuration/model/container/business mutations.
checks: Read complete attempt4-to5 delta. T5 is exactly six constant/path replacements (state5/helper5/branch5/parent38f2e31986006e5cf41f383e726abff04a2e86ef/sourceReview5/reservation5); plan/hash/three-file/single-dispatch/first-attempt/normal-workflow/canonical-result controls are identical.

Collector PIN=False remains frozen. Only classify changes and two pure bounded extraction functions are added; all readSQL/readonly/retention/sealed/source/current/iso/private/main/collect functions are AST-identical to attempt4. Raw error hash and bytes calculation remains unchanged.

technical_text visits values only, never object keys or numeric values; max depth4,16 visited values,2048 chars per leaf and8192 total. This avoids masking an entire JSON wrapper while allowing finite technical messages inside value leaves.

technical_tokens outputs only exact SOURCE_IDS or IDENTIFIERS, or lowercased fixed TECH_WORDS. Ordered output is capped at64 known tokens/96 sequence tokens; every unknown chunk becomes the constant[REDACTED], never an arbitrary captured substring or value.

Quoted strings remain hidden unless their entire interior exactly equals a static SOURCE_ID. URLs/emails/paths are masked before token lookup. Whole chunks are compared without splitting high-entropy values into keyword fragments. Single-quote opening requires a nonword boundary, preserving later finite tokens after contractions while leaving the contraction itself redacted.

Static SOURCE_IDS are bounded source/schema/function identifiers from analysis handler/helpers; no dynamic business names, record IDs, model values, request questions, SQL identifiers outside the fixed list or provider addresses are permitted output.

All prior diagnostic scope and guards remain: fixed dual services/window/routes, all route candidates regardless method/status, sanitized finite status/type/method, strict2xx metadata-only,4selected archive database seals, read-only live transactions, numeric-only coverage/retention, before-after runtime/source checks and private bounded safe receipts.

No raw headers/query/user/questions/business/provider content is saved or printed, no HTTP/model/config/container/business action is introduced. Prior frozen attempts and their receipts remain separate.

cases: Dictionary value fixture recovers invalid sort field inspect_date, resolve field staff,GoError,missing named parameter start while excluding dynamic object keys, secrets,quoted business values,URLs/emails/paths and arbitrary numbers. Exact quoted static IDs survive; unknown quoted values and whole high-entropy chunks remain hidden; traversal/output caps pass.

AST/text comparison proves only classifier+two pure extractors change and T5 is six constants only. All prior read/runtime/SQL/archive/seal/retention/iso/private/main guards unchanged; no broad suite rerun.

validationBoundaries: This is a read-only diagnostic review, not an incident root-cause conclusion; actual collection results must be interpreted after the new run.
Four sources are separately observed read transactions, not a global point-in-time database snapshot. Only selected archive evidence is rehashed, not the entire release archive.

100-record-per-source and final byte limits can omit records; counts/limited flags/outputRecordsOmitted remain explicit. Empty retained logs cannot disprove the incident or distinguish deletion, retention, disabled logging and missing historical coverage without further evidence.
Coverage/retention values describe observed log availability and settings; they do not prove the exact cause/time/actor of missing rows. Hook-replaced upstream error details cannot be reconstructed.
No real model request, production login, business write or configuration change is performed or inferred by this review.

Logged status is an internal observed field;0/nonstandard/null does not by itself establish the actual HTTP or upstream provider response. Actual root-cause conclusions require the new safe error classifications.

Finite tokens are partial technical clues, not raw error reconstruction or proof of root cause. Input depth/node/leaf/character bounds and token limits can omit content; technicalTokenOutputTruncated describes output token limits, not complete raw-error traversal.
